title: The Elder Who Refuses to Retire

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An old builder insists on climbing roofs despite a recent fall: let them keep working, or find a safer job together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has thatched roofs for fifty years and fell off one last month. (subject.He/she) is fine, mostly, and is already back on a ladder. (friend), (subject.his/her) apprentice, is terrified (subject.he/she) will fall again. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) holds the ladder every time. (subject) works slower, and more carefully, and keeps thatching. (friend) learns more in that season than in the five before it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks (subject) to teach from the ground instead, shouting instructions up to the young thatchers. (subject) grumbles that it is not the same. It is not. (subject.He/she) turns out to be a very loud and very good teacher.
